svg.title: The two supercomputers, to scale, and one JANUS run
svg.desc: Left: Deucalion and MareNostrum 5 as blocks of node squares, one square for 32 nodes, with the partitions used by the allocations filled in, and bars comparing their peak performance of 9.76 and 314 petaflops. Right: a run as four stages, parallel file system, CPU nodes under a Slurm job array, GPU nodes running the JANUS ensemble, and the catalogue written back, with the two FCT allocations tabulated below.
svg.text: THE TWO MACHINES, TO SCALE: ONE SQUARE IS 32 NODES
Guimarães, Portugal; hosted by FCT, run with CNCA, INESC TEC and U. Minho
2 x AMD EPYC 7742, 128 cores a node
10.6 PB parallel file system, 430 TB NVMe
4 x NVIDIA H100 64 GB a node
one petaflop is a million billion calculations a second
ONE JANUS RUN ON THE MACHINES
1,500 A100 GPU-hours = one 4-GPU node for 16 days
1,000 H100 GPU-hours = one 4-GPU node for 10 days
Node-days are arithmetic: core-hours over the cores of one node, over 24 hours.
